food_consumption.fish: Never or less than once a month

masculine_norms.construct: Traditional masculinity norms measured with the Male Role Norms Inventory (MRNI; Levant et al., 1992), subscales: avoidance of femininity, restrictive emotionality, aggression, achievement status, self-reliance, and attitudes toward sex (54 items; homophobia subscale excluded).
masculine_norms.direction: Higher scores indicate stronger endorsement of traditional masculine norms.

masculinity_of_meat.construct: Perceived masculinity of meat measured with the 7-item Masculinity of Meat scale (Lax & Mertig, 2020; e.g. 'Men need to eat meat more than women do').
masculinity_of_meat.direction: Higher scores indicate stronger perceived masculinity-meat link and anti-vegetarian bias.

meat_attachment.construct: Meat attachment measured with a 5-item shortened form of the Meat Attachment Questionnaire (Graca et al., 2015; e.g. 'Meat is irreplaceable in my diet').
meat_attachment.direction: Higher scores indicate stronger emotional and habitual attachment to eating meat.

dairy_attachment.construct: Dairy attachment measured on an identical scale to meat attachment, with 'dairy' replacing 'meat' (Graca et al., 2015 adaptation).
dairy_attachment.direction: Higher scores indicate stronger emotional and habitual attachment to dairy consumption.

vegetarianism_threat.construct: Perceived threat from the rise of vegetarianism measured with the 8-item Vegetarianism Threat Scale (Dhont & Hodson, 2014; e.g. 'The rise of vegetarianism poses a threat to our country s cultural customs').
vegetarianism_threat.direction: Higher scores indicate stronger perceived societal or cultural threat from vegetarianism.
vegetarianism_threat.rescaling_note: Values in the dataset appear rescaled from the original 1–5 to 1–7 range, likely for comparability with other constructs.

simulation_config.notes: Recruited as a regular meat eater.
